units.source_text: 音乐似梦，同时也与梦相反，类似更加确实的觉醒的状态。

en.t: Music resembles a dream, yet at the same time it is the opposite of a dream, something like a more certain state of awakening.

units.source_text: 我在思索：音乐究竟属于哪一类呢？

en.t: I wondered: to which category does music really belong?

units.source_text: 不管怎么说，有时音乐具备可以使这两种相反的东西逆转的力量。

en.t: In any case, at times music has the power to reverse these two opposing things.

units.source_text: 有时我很容易地化身为我自己吹奏的《源氏车）的曲调。

en.t: At times I easily transformed into the melody of Genji-guruma that I myself was playing.

units.source_text: 我懂得我的精神化身为音乐的乐趣。

en.t: I understood the pleasure of my spirit transforming into music.

units.source_text: 与柏木不同，音乐对我确是一种慰藉。

en.t: Unlike Kashiwagi, music was indeed a form of solace for me.
